newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian state workers unionise, demand raises.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian state workers unionise, demand raises.

text.p: Cambodian state employees formed their first free trade union in more than two decades on Saturday, marking the occasion with a demonstration for higher wages.

More than 100 workers from the military, police and civil service held placards and chanted slogans in front of the national cabinet for over an hour under light security, snarling traffic and drawing dozens of bystanders.
"I make only 50,000 riel ($18.50) per month, and that is not enough to support my family," said Pinsu, 25, a soldier and member of the newly formed Free Trade Union of Khmer Civil Servants.
The union, which is headed by a university teacher and claims 190 members, issued a statement at the protest requesting a wage increase of almost $4 per month, their first raise since 1993.

But the legal status of the new union is in doubt. The civil service law outlaws unions, and the draft labour law, which gives workers the right to unionise, does not cover civil servants, legal experts say.
The constitution, by contrast, contains an article giving all workers the right to organise.
The demonstration and union were organised by the opposition Khmer Nation Party (KNP), led by Sam Rainsy, a former finance minister who advocates higher government salaries.

Low- and mid-level government workers average under $20 per month in Cambodia, below the per capita average income of about $25 and far beneath the wages of top officials, who receive $1,000 to $2,500 per month.
